preamble: Nasal assimilation of [t] to [n] occurs when a stop immediately precedes a nasal and the velum lowers early, so the oral closure is kept but released through the nose. Korean applies this obligatorily before nasals (낱말 nat-mal > [nanmal]), and Latin shows the same assimilation historically in Proto-Italic *atnos > annus 'year'.

examples.note: Obligatory regressive nasalization: the neutralized coda stop [t̚] becomes [n] before the nasal [m]; 낱말 'word' is pronounced [nanmal] (phonetic hangul 난말).
The cluster *tn assimilated to nn; cf. Gothic aþn- (ataþni), Oscan akno-, Umbrian acnu.

sources: Sohn, H.-M. (1999). The Korean Language. Cambridge University Press. https://www.cambridge.org/9780521361231
